Good quality, good price, very effective (pleasantly surprised). Bare-bones, just the tools and a case, but the tools are of pretty good quality (I was pleasantly surprised). The sparse packaging is typical of stuff from Asia (just a guess), but you also get the lower price that comes with that. I prefer it that way (less stuff in the landfill).

If you're expecting a manual with it, then this product is probably not for you, safety-wise, and I mean that most respectfully. I guess it might say "Insert in ear, please be super careful". This is the kind of thing they usually don't sell in the US (at least from a big company) due to liability. Especially with the ear, the rule is "Only let a doctor do it" (like it is for so many things). Let me tell you, the doctors I've seen don't want to do it either (would you?). They give you the 'yuk, that's beneath me' look and refer you to earwax drops (which never worked for us). I guess what I mean is that if you're looking at buying this, you've probably tried to clean your ear with other (usually unsuitable) objects (Q-tips, etc) without much success, so you have some experience on what's safe to do and how you might use this. Again, you have to be super careful.

Now my short experience with this is to clean out the wax of another (elderly) person, not my own. I don't need it (yet), tho I suspect it's much more effective when you can see what you're doing, which you cant on yourself. Also, I think by restricting your cleaning to what you can see, you're less likely to go too deep (like you might on yourself). It works really well on dry, flaky wax. On more wet, viscous wax, I cant say. Compared to what I've used before, it's no contest. I'm really happy with it. So much more wax than I've been able to get out before.

There are three tools, each with its own usefulness that is apparent or you can figure out as you go. One is for (dull) scraping (looks like a round paw), one is for twisting/catching loose stuff (bulb-shaped spring), and one seems like a combo of both (looks like a mace w/three ridges). The last one has edges that are a little sharp, which you might need (use gently), but can be painful on the delicate skin of the inner ear. I've seen bleeding from using a Q-tip too much, so be careful.

I would clean these after every use. I use isopropyl alcohol (cheap from walmart).

The plastic case is plain and flimsy, like a throwaway case, but is actually very useful (so don't toss it). You need something to hold the tools, and it's just the right size and transparent too. I need to get better at opening it (press down where the single retaining tab is). There's plenty of places for air to get in to allow the tools to dry. Convenient.

Amazing product to keep long beautiful hair. I've been using this ( I mix half of this with half baby face pure protein)or a few years and have very long thick color treated blonde hair. This is the prettiest, longest and thickest that I've had my hair. I've used everything to try and stop breakage and split end. This is amazing as long as you know how it works. It restores lost hair protein due to processing (coloring bleaching)and styling. Let me go over the basics.

This doesn't work alone you need to mix with the best conditioner you can(crappy conditioner will give you crappy results). Sulphates strip out protein so change to sulphate free shampoo if you want this to work. Do not just put this on your hair with nothing mixed in it. Oils mixed with it, without any conditioner, don't increase the effectiveness. Do not use the whole bottle. Do not use every week unless you're at a place where all of your hair is breaking off.

So here's how to use it. Use a sulphate clarifying shampoo (suave clarifying is fine) to strip hair from styling products and excess protein from this treatment if you've used it before. Next towel dry your hair and mix a cap of protein into the best conditioner you have. Put the mix in your hair making sure to comb through (if your hair is short, for longer hair just massage into all your hair)to ensure all is covered. I leave it about 30 minutes. Rinse out after that(don't wash). The protein can make the hair a wee bit sticky when wet after treating. I find this happens less with baby face brand than with Protein RX but this gives you that gorgeous shine, baby face gives no shine. I find protein RX makes it a bit tacky (it can make you think it's damaged, especially if there's a weak area it's helping to strengthen) but don't cut off hair thinking it's damaged. The protein just needs to cure. So blow dry your hair until dry or close, no tugging or running a brush through while wet. I use a pick to comb through. You can slightly dry and let air dry if you want. When your hair is bone dry (never use hot tools on damp hair) harden the protein more by using your styling tool. Flat iron all your hair if you flat iron. Curl all your hair if you're into curling. Use your normal heat setting, do not crank it up to 450 thinking that will work better. Leave it 48 hours before washing in sulphate free shampoo and conditioner. You are letting the protein harden during the 48 hours.

I use it every 4 weeks. If it's been two weeks and I'm getting my hair bleached/colored I use it directly after. It works better after a process than before.

You are wasting your money if you put this in and then use sulphate shampoo. The sulphate filled shampoo is fine when clarifying and reapplying. Use it with a quality deep conditioner. Do not just mix this with defrizzing products and wonder why it doesn't work. Do not just apply a bottle of this to your head and wonder why it's sticky but doesn't help. This is not the expensive salon keratin straightener that leaches formaldehyde and is hard on your hair, it's better and safer. It is a great safe product to give you amazing hair but it will leave the wave or curl that is naturally in your hair. It does make your hair healthier.

It will not make your hair grow that is up to your body. It will not fix split end, they need to be cut off. It does prevent breakage and split end. It's essential if you color, perm or style your hair constantly. If you don't like how it feels (you've used too much and hair feels sticky) it's easily removable by a few sulphate shampoo and add baking soda while shampooing. Once you've used it took be hooked on how great it is and how great your hair looks. I make sure I've used this at least 3 weeks before a process and immediately after to avoid damage.

Answering a few questions:
what's the difference between this and babyface protein? Babyface is just protein but no added aminos or such that help the hair. Babyface will not add shine. I mix half and half.
Does the quality of conditioner and shampoo matter? For clarifying before treating a cheap sulphate shampoo is fine. For the conditioner, it completely matters so something good from Amazon, tjmaxx or marshals (if you're on a budget there are some great discount buys Dermorganics, bed head and such) is a great option. It only made my hair a little softer..... I bought this at Sally Beauty. I am caucasion, in my 50's with blonde/gray fine hair that is straight with some body & has never been colored or bleached; length is 2" below my shoulders.
My hair has been very dry for a long time despite lots of moisturizing, a salon keratin treatment (cha-ching!), argon oil, deep conditioning, etc... This Aphogee two-step protein treatment was recommended to me at the Sally Beauty store, and I figured it was worth a try. I followed the instructions to a T & also watched lots of youtube videos. I used this today exactly as directed & with high hopes. I shampooed & towel-dried my hair, then applied protein treatment, blow dried my hair for 12 minutes w/ the protein treatment in it, then rinsed in shower with warm water followed by the balancing moisturizer for at least 2 minutes, rinsed & used a moisturizing hair mask ("Mystic Divine" Coconut Complex Hydrating Masque), then rinsed again. My hair felt softer, at first, but my frizzies & curly gray hairs are still sticking out all over. I didn't get any more body in my hair either (my keratin treatment was last year 2017). So, all in all it is okay as a moisturizer, but no better than a regular deep moisture conditioner or mask. I'm not sure if I would use it again, maybe. I'm glad I just got the sampler size.
Here are my tips:
1) Use a spray mister bottle for the protein liquid & make sure you get out every last drop from the packet because most of it came out as beer colored water, then at the bottom of the packet was more of a thick cream, so I shook them together in the spray bottle & I'm so glad I used that! Don't just pour it on your head, at the very least pour a little into your hands at a time (after massaging the packet to mix contents) and smooth through your hair that way. There was just enough for my hair length.
2) Don't put a towel or anything around your shoulders, no clothing either because the protein treatment will dry your hair to it. Don't pull your stuck hairs off your skin, they'll come unattached in the shower, no worries. I kept my hair behind me to apply treatment & blow dry.
3) After drying the protein into your hair, don't touch your hair or bend it, (you can very gently touch lightly with your finger, if you hair wasn't already super brittle; it will feel like plastic sort of. 4) Be very careful blow-drying; I pointed the dryer downward alternating between medium & high heat & kept it farther from my hair so it wasn't blowing it around as it hardened. When hair is totally hard & dried through then gently let the shower water fall over all of your hair until you feel no more stiffness, then you can condition.
It's worth a try! The packets were just under $4 at Sally Beauty if you want to try it, or order here on Amazon.

Great for My Natural Nails. I was looking for a manicure device for natural nails. According to other reviewers, this doesn’t work well on acrylic or gel, which I’ve never used, so I thought I would give it a try on my natural nails. It was a good decision! It was also a good price, which was helpful since I have never used one and only heard of “nail drills” when I searched for emery boards. I couldn’t figure out who would want to drill their nails! It sounded like a torture device! It turned out to be easy and painless.

This is a great little manicure kit. I got it yesterday, charged it, and tried it today. It’s very easy to use. The instruction manual told me everything I needed to know to use it, including that it shuts off after two minutes, but you can simply turn it back on. For me, that’s not a problem. It is not faulty if it shuts off after two minutes. It’s supposed to do that. The device has two speeds, and it can reverse directions.

I was concerned about vibration, but this didn’t vibrate noticeably to me. I really dislike using an emery board or other manual file because it feels uncomfortable. Filing with this little machine was so much better. It even has a light that shines on the work area. I also used the fine sander to smooth my nails, and then polish them. It was very easy, and the shine is amazing.

It is rechargeable through USB. It comes with a cord that has a special end to plug into the manicure tool. The other end plugs into a USB wall charger which is not supplied. Again, for me that was not a problem as I have quite a few of those in the house.

The kit comes with 1 grinder to file nails, 2 coarse sandpaper disks, 2 fine nail file boards (look similar to sandpaper disks, but much finer), and 2 EVA polish rollers. It also has a small bag of 10 extra assorted sticker, of the types I just mentioned. I am not sure how long each one lasts or how to order more if I need them. I couldn’t find the information in the Amazon description or in the manual that came with the kit. I’ll keep looking.

I charged this in the bedroom overnight. When charging, the device has a light that flashes during charging, but stops flashing and remains on once charged. It’s pretty bright on a nightstand in a dark bedroom. I’ll probably charge it during the day! The first charge took about three hours.

I hope this continues working as well as it did on my first try. As of now, I highly recommend this MiroPure kit. If that changes for any reason, I will update this post.

Nice, silicone back 'brush' bit too soft. Good handles.. We gave this 3 test uses for an initial assessment of this back scrubber/brush. It is designed nicely, with handles that make usage very user friendly. If they made this out of elastic, you could shower and do resistance band exercises. hehe. Seriously, the handles work well, and act as convenient loops to hang the device to dry out in the shower.
There is an issue with using silicone brush heads, they tend to be soft/flexible. So, if you use this brush, do not expect the same experience as a loofah or bristle brush. And, you have to really work up a lather in your hands and then transfer it to the silicone brush head. Attempts to create foam/lather by rubbing body wash or soap on the silicone just wasn't satisfactory.
As mentioned, the brush surface tends to be soft/gentle. The 'scrubbing' side does rub, but nowhere near deep cleaning or exfoliating level. The bumpy side, for massage, does provide a textured rub, but is even less effective for soaping and cleaning your back.
Maybe I'm too old school, liking my cleaning brush to be able to really scrub.
Attached are photos to show real world images, with a ruler for size reference.
Did not use the included hooks, because we used the shower caddy that already had hooks for shower accessories. The bonus bath sponge looks fine, but did not use that yet. Again, maybe I don't pamper myself enough while showering. haha. If the significant other uses it, any pertinent information will be added to this review. However, I think the majority of people will be concerned about the effectiveness and quality of the back scrubber.
So, the product does match the description and depiction in the product details. However, my opinion is the softness of the brush hinders the effectiveness as a shower back scrubbing device. I do like that it is very resistant to mold and is extremely easy to clean and maintain. Maybe I have to learn to adapt to the softer texture of this type of brush. Based on our experience, this silicone brush garners a 3.5 rating. If you already use and like silicone back scrubbers, this is a quality product worth considering. If you are old school, this might disappoint expectations.

I would recommend going slow, especially if it's your first time applying nail wraps. The secret is to lightly buff the top of your nail to give the wrap something with texture to adhere to. Then, wash your hands throughly and wipe your nails down with an alcohol pad to get any excess natural oil off of them. This will also help it stick longer because oil will break down the adhesive. Then, start at the base of your nail and slowly apply, pulling only slightly enough for the strip to remain taut.  When you get to the end of your nail, pinch the strip together so it wraps around the edges and push over and under the edge slightly so it's wrapped the front completely as well. Use your finger to smooth out any wrinkles  (usually it's very few, if any), then lightly and slowly file off the excess in a downward motion instead of a side to side motion. Hit with the blow dryer for a few seconds and you're good to go! I gave nails that last 14+ days doing it this way, and the incoco ones are seriously great for it.

-guidelight

-nice cleaning tools and storage bag

Cons
-charge lasts 20-25 min at most, definitely NOT 40 min as advertised

-this does NOT pluck hairs that are 0.5 mm in length; in fact it will cut many longer hairs and leave them at 0.5-1 mm, unable to remove them no matter how many times you run the epilator over them
-the massaging brush is too soft to exfoliate anything at all, better to use a loofah/manual brush

Overall:
This is an average epilator, definitely not worth $100. I might return this and get an Emjoi.

coming from someone whose had pro 28 full body laser removal treatments and 50 hrs of electrolysis. Needless to say i have xp with hair removal. I was never really a super hairy but loved the feeling of being totally hairless from head to toe.

With all the sessions and hrs i barley have any hair but do have some spots on thighs, arms and other spots, that are fairly light even with all the professional laser treatments and electrolysis. IPL aka this device is NOT the go-to treatment for hair reduction but it does work.

Firstly, you need to use an electric razor or standard razor on the areas your zapping. Freshly showered, no oils or lotions on skin. If you dont feel heat your not killing hair follicles. The laser targets the pigment in the hair and absorbs the heat, so as they stated vampire skin, dark hair gets the best results.

If you have never gotten any sort of pro hair removal your hair is going to be fuller and courser. Like the subject heading states, ive had 28 full body laser hair removal treatments aka real hair removal that leaves you with red bumps, plus hrs of electrolysis and I still have hair grow back.

People it takes a long time to remove hair! This is not designed to be a one zap and the hair is gone. It will grow back finer and weaker, until it eventually is killed off. It literally takes years.

I zap each spot 5 times on the highest setting. The heat will build on each subsequent zap, meaning im actually hitting follicles. I would not recommend this if you have course hair or never had pro hair removal - build up to that, but this device is a nice supplement to the pro hair removal. It will never replace it and will take longer. For me its perfect and thats why i gave it 5 stars.

Once you zap the hair you should see a reaction, raised bumps, some redness, along the bikini line for example its very noticeable since the hair is courser - that means its working. It takes about 10 -14 days for the zapped hair to push its way out. Its not instant, the hair still remains in the follicle. You can expedite this by lightly exfoliating in the bath or shower. You may see little black spots in the follicle where the hair has been zapped and effectively targeted.

Hair grows in cycles, doing this every week is pointless, if the hair is not in the growth phase you cant kill it. Every 4 weeks, multiple zaps per spot and the hair WILL fall out and come back weaker. Different areas have different growth cycles but 4 weeks is a good middle ground.

This is used for hair reduction. If you want permanent (still takes multiple treatments( you need electrolysis.

If you want faster hair reduction result you need to use laser only found at the dermatologist or reputable laser spa. IPL is not laser treatment. This is not going to ever replace that. A combination of all three over 3 or 4 years will leave you hairless, so keep your expectations realistic.

Feels premium and great performance. Met all my criteria. Can't say enough good things.. I'm a guy, but I was looking for something that will (hopefully) last long. I initially thought I had simple/easily found criteria for a new hair dryer, but I had trouble meeting them. Based on my previous hair dryer ownership, I noticed there were 2 failures that would come up first, switch failure or motor fan failure. My criteria was looking for a switch that operates like a toggle switch and had the 2 speeds on either end of the off position (LOW - OFF - HIGH). My reasoning for the switches is that the sliding type switch tends to wear out faster. Less cycling of the switch to reach the HIGH setting increases my chance of longer ownership. My other criteria is that it needs to have an AC type motor, rather than the cheaper/low durability DC motor. This hair dryer met them all!

At first feel, the lightly rubber body coating was nice, felt premium and not sticky. Weight was on the heavier side compared to the cheaper models I owned before. Quality electronics tend to be heavier and an indication of quality materials. When I first turned it on, I noticed it sounded like those found in salons, and the motor felt and sounded strong (lots of torque). Fan flow was also strong. 3 heat settings made it fully adjustable. I found that some of the attachments had trouble staying attached, especially the comb. I liked the fact that it comes with a filter. A nice feature is that it comes with a Velcro loop for cable management. Some other interesting thing is that there's a small blue LED on top when the hair dryer is on. The infrared bulb turns on in the Medium and High heat settings, there's no option to turn this off. It does dry my hair quickly and my hair does feel better/softer compared to my previous hair dryer.

If you are initially looking for a hair dryer in the $20-30 range, definitely consider this! It is worth the extra money. Don't let the not well known brand deter you.

Side by side comparison of three sleep masks-Earth Theraputics is no longer my favorite. This is a side-by-side comparison of three masks:
[[ASIN:B001ET7HJI Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Sleep Mask, Cotton, Silk]]
[[ASIN:B00FJQFJX8 Bedtime Bliss® Contoured & Comfortable Sleep Mask & Moldex® Ear Plugs]]
[[ASIN:B00M9BC1M8 Premium Quality Eye Mask with Contoured Shape By Nidra]]

I've used the Earth Therapeutics soft mask for five years, and the the Nidra and Bedtime Bliss masks for the last several months. All have their advantages and disadvantages. My favorite is now the Nidra mask, but it has an important flaw.

I sleep from after midnight until 8am, and my bedroom is bright. Therefore, I need a mask that will stay on for seven or eight hours. If it shifts when I move during the night, it will not be covering my eyes when the sun comes up.

Although I used it for several years, the Earth Therapeutics mask does the worst job of staying in place all night. I think this is because it does not have as much shape or structure as the other two masks. Also, it presses on your eyes, making it a bit less comfortable than the other two masks. I no longer use this mask.

The Nidra mask does the best job of staying in place. It is also slightly larger than the Bedtime Bliss mask, and feels a bit more comfortable. However, the Nidra has a flaw: Although they all have the same length band, the elastic on the Nidra band has a bit more tension than the Bedtime Bliss or the Earth Therapeutics masks, which means that it is too tight on my fat head. I have actually had to extend the strap with a piece of dual-sided velcro strap in order to make it comfortable. Now it fits the best and stays in place better than the other two masks.

The Nidra mask is about 3/4 inch or 2cm wider across the eyes than the Bedtime Bliss mask. If you have a small or narrow face, you may want to try the Bedtime Bliss mask first

As far as light blocking and comfort go, both the Nidra and the Bedtime Bliss do a good job. Therefore, my choice is the Nidra because it stays on better after I make the strap longer.

Summary: I have stopped using the Earth Therapeutics mask. The Bedtime Bliss and Nidra are very similar, but the Nidra fits me better and stays in place longer. If you have a large head like me, the Nidra mask will be tight. If you have a small or narrow face, try Bedtime Bliss.

The other thing that might dent the value for the cost is that I suspect that some will be left over at the bottom of the container, just like there's always leftover stick deodorant. But who knows? It’s Okay, But Not For Me.... This is okay but there’s a few issues I have with it....

First, the mirror came with a little chunk in the corner gone. It’s not a big deal because it’s so small, but it would be nice if the mirror would have come better protected so that it wasn’t missing a piece no matter how small.

Second, this doesn’t really hold much unless you want it to be all separate parts. If you have it all put together with the side trays sitting on each side of the big oval tray, the silicone pieces over top the side trays, and the square tray sitting in the middle of the big oval tray - Then you can’t hold much with it. The side trays with the silicone pieces only hold so much. The one with the lines you can lay brushes in the grooves like shown in the photos on the product page. But, there’s only 4 grooves where brushes can actually lay, and more than 1 or sometimes 2 brushes is all that fits in each groove. The other silicone tray has the X’s that you can put things in so they stand straight up. There’s 11 small ones and 8 big ones. The big ones you could potentially fit more than 1 item in. Also, the middle tray part that the mirror goes over as a lid, if you’re going to do that, then you can only have items in that tray that the mirror will be able to lay flat over, so that limits how much and what you can place in it. If you have it all put together, then it doesn’t take up much room. But, if you have it all in separate parts (like the first photo on the product page), then it takes up a lot of room for not holding too much. I might as well keep using my cups or brush holders for my brushes, which hold a ton of brushes, and plastic or acrylic drawer organizers.

Third, I don’t like how the mirror just sits, it isn’t actually attached. It comes off so easy. One little bump and the mirror falls over. It would be nice if they would have that attached somehow so that it would fold down over the tray but still be connected.

Finally, it’s supposed to be easy to wash and dry. To me, the silicone pieces are not easy to clean. The dust collects on them like crazy. And I try to just wipe off the dust with a dry cloth but the silicone is rubbery and the dust just kind of sticks to it. If you use a wet cloth you’re able to get the dust, but you have to work really hard to get it off. I just don’t like it.

Overall, this just doesn’t work for me. I wanted it to organize things while taking up less space. But, when it is taking up less space, it doesn’t hold enough for me. If you’re looking just to hold a few small things. Like you have some small items that you just want to have a place, then this might work for you. As long as you don’t mind that the mirror isn’t attached and might come off easy.

Will power laptop and still has two usb charging ports.. This is a review of the Silicon Devices 150W High Performance Auto Power Inverter.

I have this in my SUV to allow me to use my laptop on the go. My laptop I use for travel is older and has no battery that keeps a charge. It also charges my phone but that need is rare as my phone battery keeps a nice charge.
For those who may not know what a power inverter is, it is a basic device that you can plug into a dc vehicle outlet and converts it so you can use an ac device. (DC outlet to AC outlet.) This one does have an extra bonus as it throws in two USB charging ports. The USB ports are rated 1amp and 2.1amp. (Use the higher one for your tablets and heavy power hungry devices.)
This takes in 12volts DC and puts out up to 150 watts which is plenty for normal ac devices such as laptops and portable electronics. It is only 9.6 oz and measures 4.3” x 3” x 1.7”. It is made of metal and is very durable so you can toss in your glove or utility box so it is ready to go. Cable is also nice and long so you can reach from front of the car to the middle area so others can use from all the other seats.

Cons – One thing I did notice is that the DC plug did not have a fuse in line. The description indicates this has over and under voltage protection; however, I am not clear if this is for the usb ports and or if this applies to the ac outlet as well. Other inverters typically offer fuses or a fuse if you remove the end cap on the dc plug. (On the up side, the soldering inside the dc plug was very nice and solid with nothing loose or questionable.)

Tips / Notes – Make sure your vehicle is running when you use this. This has potential to draw a good deal of power if using the upper range of 150watts and can run down your battery if the vehicle is not on allowing your alternator to prevent battery drainage.

Summary – This works as described and is very small. It has a built in fan to keep this cool as it works. It is very quiet and does what is expected. I would recommend this to friends and family.

Excellent results, just be patient!. I have tried a number of lash lengthening products over the years, most provided very modest results at best. This one is different, and I can testify that about 10 weeks after starting, my lashes and eyebrows have lengthened and thickened considerably.
It does feel a bit silly to be applying this colorless liquid in a thin line right over the lash line day after day without seeing any difference! But around weeks 6 to 7, I could see that the base of my lashes looked darker and thicker, and that the little bald patches at the end of my eyebrows now had definition and that new eyebrow hair was growing. My lashes are now longer than when I was a teenager, and an extremely light application of mascara is all that is needed for going out, I am planning on no mascara at all in a few more weeks. More and I might risk the Tammy Faye Baker look!
To apply, I use a good quality eyeliner brush dedicated to this purpose (no need for it to be disposable, just position it so it can air dry) and place one to two drops of solution in a contact lens solution cap. I do apply it to top and lower lashes, sparingly but so it looks wet. One drop is plenty for lashes, the second is mostly for my eyebrows.
I have not found the product to re-pigment the skin, nor has it created any irritation. One bottle lasted for about 8 weeks, it would obviously last longer with a one drop application. I will be continuing this regimen, probably switching to every other day in a few weeks. Call me very pleased!

Day 2: The skin on my feet is noticeably tight. The left foot has very slight flaking around the toes and the right foot has a spot starting to obviously peel. Took a shower, no extra attention to the feet other than regular wash and now there is obvious peeling on both feet. Day 3: noticeable itchiness and more peeling to be had on the soles of my feet. Day 4: Ok, this peeling is gross! Holy smokes, everything is peeling it even feels like the tops of my feet may start peeling. Day 5: OMG all the peeling. Day 6: Peeling has calmed down on the bottom of the foot and around the toes but the tops of the feet haven’t started at all but it looks and feels like it is going to. Day 7: I cheated. I soaked my feet and gave them a very light pumice scrub to get the skin from the tops of my feet off and to touch up a dry patch on one heel. Final verdict: totally worth it. Recommendations: After reading through use and reviews of other similar products, I would recommend soaking your feet every day. It may help avoid the issue I had with the skin on the tops of my feet.

There is much to like here, but there are some reservations. There is much to like here, but there are some reservations. Some reviewers suggested an instruction booklet, shave cream, and blades. This would appear to be a bit too much --- if you don't know how to shave, why are you buying this set. But, I do note that it is being marketed as for beginner shavers. It might be sensible to put in the description that blades and shave cream will have to be purchases separately. Amazon might even pick up some additional business.

It is not easy to see the razor that comes with this set; it is a three piece closed bar razor. Schone is not a well known brand, and the little that is known of them usually revolves around an open comb Italian style razor, this is not it. Also, they keep describing the brush that comes with the kit as synthetic badger. There is really no such thing. This is a synthetic brush that is made to look like badger. There is no reason to confuse this issue.

Well then, what is good here and why four stars. After these few quibbles, I found the set to be excellent. Both the razor and the shave brush have solid metal handles, which fit perfectly with the stand that comes with them. The razor is solid and mildly aggressive: it is reminiscent of the popular Edwin Jaeger DE89. Solid and heavy, with just the right blade exposure, it give a marvelous shave. And the shave brush works up a substantial lather with little effort. Synthetic brushes are not always good, this one is great. However, a new shaver might want a milder razor. Anyone who is an experienced shaver would love this set. In my opinion, the razor or the shave brush alone would easily be worth the whole price of this set. This is a great deal.

Not bad. I'm surprised by all the bad reviews of this product. I had a pretty good experience with it overall. I liked the foam application and the color is very nice. It burned my scalp a bit, which is not unusual for me with permanent hair color (I did not do the allergy test beforehand). It seemed to dry my hair, but I have dry hair to begin with and all permanent colors seem kind of harsh. I prefer semi-perm colors, but my hair is getting too gray to use those any longer. After I used the conditioner with this product and my hair dried, it looked fine, shiny even. I thought it did a pretty good job of coloring my gray.

Some of the bad reviewers sound like they are new to hair coloring. I learned years ago that you have to go with a lighter shade than you think you need. The first time I colored my hair Medium Brown, it came out looking black, and I had to wait several months to grow it out and let it fade before I could try again. When I called the L'Oreal (or Clairol, I don't remember which) help line, they told me that I should have used a lighter color. I don't know why this isn't spelled out more clearly in the instructions, but they seem to think that you should know that already. If you're new to coloring your own hair, you might want to call one of the help lines first, or experiment with semi-perm colors. I would describe my hair as Medium Brown, but I use light brown or even a dark blonde hair color. "Brown" or "Golden Brown" will have reddish tones; if you don't want any red, try an "Ash" color.

I used the Light Golden Brown with this product and it came out as almost (but not quite) Auburn, which is what I was shooting for. I think it's a very nice, natural looking color. I may alternate with semi-perm colors to try to save my hair from turning to straw, but I will probably use the product again.

Basically, the kitchen sink of hair misery. For these reasons, I wore a short pixie for many years but grew it out when the salons were closed in 2020. Now I have a bob and product has been such an expensive hot or miss learning curve I've thought about cutting it all off again. I tried Verb Ghost on a recommendation from a friend and can definitively say it's the reason I have kept my hair longer. The shampoo has a very rich lather that cleans thoroughly but doesn't over dry. The conditioner is buttery (like a light hair mask) and leaves my hair feeling moisturized but with no weight at all and no oily scalp. With both products, a little goes a long way. The scent is incredible and - this is critical - refreshingly light. Overwhelming scents have been a big problem for me with longer hair. I was so impressed with the shampoo and conditioner, I ordered several other products from the Ghost and Volume lines with equally impressive results. I'm a fan.

Of note, like some other reviewers, my order arrived with some shipping damage (shipped by Amazon, not Verb) but I called Amazon and they made it right immediately.

This curler however is rock solid in it's build! The metal is thick and reinforced as is the connection. Another thing I preferred over the Shu Uemura is that this is strongly spring loaded where as Shu Uemura isn't.

The finger holds are very comfortable and smooth plus, also importantly, the curler looks classy! The pad on this curler, as said by the company doesn't need to be replaced. This is impressive as you can tell by looking at it and feeling it the pad is thick and does not have a lot of give to it but is still gentle enough not to harm your lashes.

As for curling. I get the curler as close to the roots as possible by about half opening my eye and the no pinch design allows you to do this easily. Then I hold for about 7 seconds occasionally pumping the curler. I then raise my eyebrows and move the curler a little farther down my lashes and pinch for a second for two while bend the curler backwards and raising the handle up a bit. The main issue with certain eyelash curlers is the over curled and bent lashes effect which also isn't good for your lashes. This curler, when not over pressed, gives a natural curler that is noticeable on it's own without even using mascara.

And a shout out to the wonderful company Bella and Bear with their wonderful customer service and wonderful products that they wholeheartedly back up! Can't go wrong here.

Works wonders for taming frizz. Smells like clove though, not citrus.. Ladies and gentlemen, let me appeal to the ladies on the great results that beard oil can have on your hair. If you have wavy, frizzy, unmanageable hair (as I do), this could really help! I had been using argan oil and other oil blends to tame my wild hair, and when I read the ingredients in my roommate's beard oil and saw how similar they were, I wanted to give it a try. I first bought the Tea Tree blend by Beardsmen Spirit, since I'm a big fan of the benefits of tea tree oil, and I liked it so much that I wanted to try out this Rousing Citrus blend.

As far as ingredients go, the Rousing Citrus blend has Jojoba seed oil, sweet almond oil, grape seed oil, glycerin, grapefruit peel oil, lemon fruit oil, blood orange essential oil, clove flower oil, and vanilla plantifolia fruit essential oil. I compared this to the ingredients in the Tea Tree blend, which are Jojoba seed oil, sweet almond oil, grape seed oil, glycerin, peppermint essential oil, tea tree leaf essential oil, and vanilla plantifolia fruit essential oil. Not too big of a difference except for the obvious different essential oils. This oil has about the same thick consistency, and a little bit goes a long way! It takes about 5-6 drops of the oil to tame the frizz in my hair that's about 4 inches down past my shoulders.

One con for me though: this oil does not really have a citrus smell. I smell clove over everything else, and while this isn't a bad thing, I was really hoping for those lemon and blood orange essential oils to be prominent. So a more appropriate name for this would be "Rousing Clove".

HORRIBLE! Tracks showing, HUUUUGE knots, hair fried!. I got the 22” Body Wave 13x4 T Part Lace.

I do NOT recommend this wig! I recommend you quickly exit out from looking at this one and find ANYTHING else! The hair is so fried! It looks and feels unhealthy! The knots are HUUUUGE! They look sooo unnatural! The top is thin so you can see the tracks. Since you only have 1” parting space, which is already the middle part, there’s no room to change it so you can’t even try to cover the tracks. There are stains inside the cap, which look to be from the combs. There are tons of dark hairs mixed throughout the hair (even though the product page said it was virgin hair, unprocessed hair. But this definitely did not come from a natural blonde. It was bleached and it wasn’t done well so it’s totally fried!). I would honestly give it zero stars if I could, but I have to give at least 1 star. I go into more detail below if you’re interested…

The product page states this is 150% density. I’m never good at determining if it’s accurate density. It honestly looks about 150% density. HOWEVER, there are areas on the top that are thin and you clearly see the tracks. Unfortunately, this is a T part Lace, so you don’t have room to change the part to cover the thin area. To me, that makes it unbearable.

The knots on this thing are INSANE! I have no clue what on earth is going on with them but they are HUGE!! They look so unnatural and ridiculous!

The product page says it is “premium hair material” and “we guarantee that T part Blonde 613 Lace Front Wig Human Hair Is 100% Real Blonde Human Hair Wigs, Soft & Healthy, No Tangle, No Shedding, Can Be Dyed, Bleached, Curled Etc.; You Can Buy without Worries.” Honestly, that is a joke! It is blonde, but it has been processed to be blonde. There are a ton of dark hairs mixed in throughout the hair. The hair has been badly bleached so it’s fried. I would never want to dye/bleach this again because I honestly don’t think the hair could take it since it’s in such bad condition! It definitely isn’t “healthy.” It’s not even really all that soft because you can feel how the hair is fried.

The hair they show on the mannequins in the product photos on the product page are definitely NOTHING like the hair I received! That hair looks soft, healthy, plucked well, and without humongous knots and tracks showing on top.

When you scroll down to the middle of the product page where they have more info. It says on the side in the grey box, “Wig Type: T Part Blonde Body Wave Virgin Human Hair Wigs.” It also says, “ Human Hair Quality: Unprocessed Brazilian Human Hair, Minimum Shedding.” “Just Like Your Own Human Hair, No Chemical.” Just full of LIES! This is NOT virgin hair. Virgin hair is also known as unprocessed hair (they mean the same thing). Unprocessed hair is human hair that has NEVER been chemically processed, this means over the life of the hair it’s never been dyed, coloured, or bleached. As a result, unprocessed hair is incredibly healthy. This has DEFINITELY been bleached so it is NOT Virgin/unprocessed. It is definitely NOT “no chemical.”

It has 13x6x1 T part lace. That means the lace goes 13” in the front ear to ear, it goes 6 inches back, and the parting space is 1”. The product page said, “T- part 13x6x1 Lace, Giving You the Ability to Have a Longer or Multi-direction Partings and Makes You More Natural.” If you know what 13x6x1 lace means, then you already knew when you purchased it that the parting space is only 1” wide. But, some people might not know what that 1 means at the end. They might see it, but then see the product page says “ability to have a longer or multi-direction partings” and think they can change the part if they want. Like I said earlier, you can NOT change this part! It is only 1” wide and that whole 1” is plucked out making the middle part. There’s no room to change it. It’s unfortunate because, like I said earlier, you can see the tracks next to the part and if you could change the part you’d have the possibility of covering them up. But, you can’t with this.

Oh, and there’s weird stains inside the cap. They look to be from the combs.

I thought it was really funny in the middle of the product page they had a little thing that said, “Are you satisfied with the 613 blonde lace front wig human hair you bought before? If not satisfied, you can try ours. Maybe we will become the terminator of your choice of blonde lace front wig human hair, and we hope to have the opportunity to become your superstar.” Become the terminator of your choice? What the heck does that mean?! 😂 They definitely are NOT going to become my superstar, or anyone else’s if they keep putting out wigs like this! Especially given the fact they’re charging $102.39 for the 18” body wave (at the time of writing this review) is crazy! It is nowhere near worth that! I definitely do NOT recommend!

Now I just reviewed this giving details about a usage that this product is not FDA approved for, so use at your own risk for bruising. Gasoline is a petroleum distillate, along with several other fuels including kerosene. Excellent shaving soap!. I bought this shaving soap, not knowing anything about "real" shaving soaps or creams. Since I started shaving, around my 13th birthday (I'm 40 now), I have always used multi-bladed cartridge razors and foamy shaving cream in a spray can. I moved to spray gels, and stayed current with the multi-blade trend. I had been using a Fusion Proglide since it came out, and before that, a plain Fusion since it hit the market. I began to notice several years ago, that shaving irritation on my neck was getting progressively worse. It got so bad, I got to where I would only shave twice a week. I tried almost every lubrication you can buy in a can for shaving, but nothing helped because my skin is so sensitive and my beard and stubble is so thick. I looked for a better cream.

I bought a cheap shaving brush and selected about 4 types of shaving soaps and creams. I happened to see this PAA Solstice, and thought it looked interesting. Once I got it and opened it, I was mesmerized by the scent. I can't accurately describe the olfactory goodness of this stuff, so I won't try. The smell was so good, I hoped it worked 1/2 as good as the scent is. Using my cheap brush, an old mug and my trusty Fusion Proglide, I whipped up the best lather a first timer could, and started to shave. Well, I actually tried a trial lather with a cream rather than this soap, but you get the idea.

At any rate, I experienced a very comfortable shave that also happened to be the closest I'd had in years. I did have mild irritation on my neck, but it was much more comfortable than anything I had tried previously. The soap lathered surprisingly well, considering i didn't really know what I was doing. It left a really slick layer to my face which helped my razor glide across my face with ease. And of course the aroma was amazing when hot water was applied to this stuff. I didn't realize it at the time, but this changed my life.

I was so thrilled by my experience with this soap, I thought now is as good a time as any to try double edged razor shaving...the old way. I bought a double edge safety razor, and even more creams and soaps. I picked up better brushes, pre-shave products, aftershave products, and an assortment of blades with which to experiment. I dove head first into traditional shaving...all because of how much I liked this soap. My skin has never been as healthy as it has been since I changed how I shave and care for my face. I still suffer mild neck irritation, but it is greatly reduced. I've added several Phoenix soaps to my shaving arsenal, and they're all great. But Solstice is by far the favorite of the bunch. I've used creams or soaps that may be better in some respects, but Solstice is an all-around performer. I rotate creams or soaps, but Solstice sees more use than anthing else in my cabinet. PAA's customer service has been A-rate also.

To put it simply, I love this shaving soap. My absolute favorite. The only complaint I have is that I liked it so much, I've invested a whole lot more into shaving than I ever thought I could...and it's all Solstice's fault! At least I like shaving again!

Spectra not Spectacular; Only its Price. I bought an expensive Norelco "Spectra" about eight weeks ago. I don't find it better than my last new and expensive Norelco, a "Quad Action," or whatever last year's "Razor-du-Jour" from Norelco was called, and I'm really disappointed.  Each year the Norelco offers less and less value.  (Ratio of quality to price.) It is not as close, and it takes longer to shave.  The only difference I can see is the little adjustment wheel, which they've had before in different forms, the pretty pearlized colors, and the the holes versus slots moved to a different location on the perimeter of each of the three circular heads. The holes are much closer shaving, as they have always been on foil razors. Norelco claims that the slots are better for "longer hairs," but if you shave every day, why would you have "longer hairs" on your face? The bottom line is that this model is NOT faster or closer than the previous one, although it's a bit smoother, but it IS more expensive. I keep buying these in the hope that each successive one is actually an improvement, rather than a marketing device with marginal changes. (And the "James Bond" tie-in promotional gift is simply, well, juvenile.  Anyone old enough to shave can see this is useless and unrelated.  A small package of pre-shave, a shaving stick, or cleaning/soaking fluid would make more sense.)  But the truth of the matter in my experience is that any of the past three major models ("Spectra," "Quad," "Reflex," whatever) are comparable if you use an appropriate pre-shave, clean the shaver often, and replace the heads as needed.  (The ability to rinse the razor clean WAS significant, however.)  The closest Norelco was the one with the micro-thin indentation in the center of each circular head around the perimeter. The fastest one had 36 (I think) cutting blades, instead of the reduced number now. (When I asked Norelco why they cut the number of blades, they said it had something to do with the "hair reservoir." What happened to the hair before?) I will continue to use Norelco, and I own three of them.  I have used them for 48 years, and they're still the best rotary razor.  But I wish they would wait for REAL improvements before releasing a new razor. (Maybe then the price wouldn't be so exorbitant, either.)

This sponge set achieves a natural looking skin! Quality product. great value.. I spent a few days before purchasing this particular silicone sponge set or any kind of silicone sponge set for that matter, but, I am very glad that I decided to give it a try! With few reviews and real life photos of the items from the customers, I hesitated to decide on ScionBeauty's sponge, but, I am a satisfied customer for the following reasons.

First of all, this is a great value for a set of 5 sponges (2 beauty blender and 3 silicone sponges). The size is not too small nor big and is perfect. Upon opening the package, I recommend washing all sponges. At least the silicone sponges. I used a very very small amount of nice hand soap and very gently washed and rinsed them well. Here are what I noticed about and did with each sponge.

** BEAUTY BLENDER:
The beauty blender indeed expand in size! I would say about 2.5 times the original size. I washed it yesterday and squeezed out excess water with a towel to make sure it doesn't build up mold inside. It did shrink, but, is still bigger than the unwashed one. And, it certainly did NOT become stiff or rip, which I was initially worried about. It became very slightly harder than the unwashed one, but, the washed one is still MUCH bouncier compared to the unwashed one. I actually like this medium level of softness/stiffness. Another reason why I hesitated to wash the blender is because I read some reviews about an inexpensive blender bleeding out pink dye. That is not the case at all about this ScionBeauty blender. At that point, I felt very comfortable using this product. When you wash it, you do need to rinse thoroughly to remove soap bubbles. If soap residue remains in the blender, the blender probably will disintegrate over time and it won't be good for your skin either. Upon arrival, the blender has a very faint smell to it. But, it does go away next day if you keep it out of a plastic bag that it comes in. Also, once you wash it, the smell completely goes away.

** SILICONE SPONGE:
It feels good against the skin! It curves well when I try to bend to fit the curves of my face, so, I can say this particular sponge is flexible. It curves but bounces back is a good way to describe it, I think. On the back side of the plastic bag this sponge set comes in, there is a sticker attached - "How to use ScionBeauty Silicone sponge." I read the instructions as well as referred to Youtube videos and online tips. You do need to dab and pat on your skin rather than glide along on your skin as they say. Then, you can successfully apply a thin and natural looking layer of liquid foundation. I like the natural look, so, this silicone sponge works well for me. Do not remove the sealing (a thin layer of silicone on the edge of the sponge). You need to use the raised side of the sponge to put foundation or any other makeup item on. I used the liquid foundation, but, all I needed was about the size (amount) of a rice grain or two and it covered about a half of my face. It did not smear (Again, dab and tap!). After I finished applying liquid foundation on my face, I again washed the silicone sponge with a very small amount of hand soap and dried with a towel. I also used the silicone sponge to apply serum and it did work extremely well. I always wasted too much with my hands soaking up the serum more than my facial skin did.

This may be a makeup fad that goes away before too long, but, I'm sure I will be using this sponge set for a long time. It was a bit disappointing that I did not receive a reply from the seller when I contacted about the warranty they mention on the Amazon product page, but, I'm sure this product will last long enough to worth the price, so, I'm ok with that in this case and decided not to deduct a star from my review. The product itself and its value still deserve 5 stars in my mind. I highly recommend this sponge set for those who are hesitating to try. It may not be your kind of item, but, if used right and if you happen to like the texture of the sponges, you will understand what I'm talking about.

I'm posting real life photos (not photoshopped, I mean) of the product, so that you can see how the sponges actually look like and how big/small they are. The sponge set does not come in a cute bag or case as you can see, but, it is good enough for yourself and casual gifting.

It is sort of a cliche, but, I DO read customer reviews very carefully before purchasing items, so, I know it is worrisome to buy an item with few reviews or from a company you have never heard of. I care about the quality over the price, but, I do care about the value, too (Is the product cost effective?). You don't have to have this sponge set, but, it really helped me and I decided to take the time to write a review here. Hopefully, my review was helpful for some of you :)

Xara 1" Infrared professional ceramic curling iron - Love it!. I recently purchased this curling iron based on what other reviewers had to say. I am very happy that I did. I have recently gone back to work in an office after several years of working from home. This means I actually have to do my hair more often. After several mornings of burning my fingers, I ditched it for a new one. And I can't get used to the gloves that you can buy to help prevent that (and never got any with that curling iron).
I am so happy with this purchase for a few reasons so far...I have not burned my fingers!! That's a pretty big reason for me!! I did receive gloves with this and I am thinking of trying them, they seem to be a better material that the ones I had before, so maybe I will get used to them. But so far, the tip hasn't gotten so hot that it burns me. Secondly, I like the temperature adjustment on this because you actually 'click' it with a button, the Baby Bliss has a dial which can easily get bumped during styling (making it too hot!) So my temp stays exactly where I want it unless I change it. And finally, the other main selling point for me was that it uses infrared light!!! Infrared light is a penetrating light and is actually less damaging. It isn't just heating the outside of the hair strands, and trust me it helps hold my curls longer. I am a brunette with med thick hair, but finer strands. Basically, my hair feels thick, but it's finer hair. And although I have natural wavy/curly hair, for some bizarre reason, it won't hold a curl from a curling iron all day. Strange, but true. Overall, it seems to be a very well constructed curling iron and I am happy I am saving the health of my finger tips and my hair from damage. I am actually going to see if they make flat irons with the infrared technology to replace my current flat iron that is acting up.

This appears to be a polyurethane material. This is not a braided multi-strand elastic that you might see on surgical masks. Rather it is a solid "rubber" material embossed with a pattern to resemble the traditional material. Technically I would call it an "elastomer", and it feels a lot like polyurethane. It is quite stretchy and will expand to roughly 250% of its non-stressed length, with very modest force. We ended up using it for several masks, but switched to the more traditional braided elastic once that finally arrived. The braided material has an inner elastomer core that is overlaid by a cotton braided covering (much like insulated wire), and then multiple strands of that are joined together side-by-side to form a ribbon. So this stuff will work if you can't get the real thing, but I might be concerned about how long it will last under repeated usage.

Great, but use before showering. I bought this trimmer after my old Norelco stopped charging. For the record, I maintain a full beard with this. Overall, I am satisfied with the product, but there are some caveats.

Vacuum: Like me, you may be interested in the included vacuum, rather than getting hair all over the place. It works pretty well for this! I'd say about 90% of the hair is trapped in the canister, about 3% on the sink, and about 7% left in my beard. For this reason, I recommend using the trimmer before you shower. Otherwise, you will get little hairs all over your shirt during the day. If you only have a goatee or similar, it may not be quite as bad. It's not much hair, but the little vacuum can't solve everything.

Noise: The noise level is loud, but not really any noisier than an electric toothbrush. To me, it's really no big deal. With the bathroom door closed, you can only hear it when close to the door anyway. I even run it in turbo mode most of the time, and still don't have an issue with this. Of course it would be great if it were completely silent, but really it's not that bad.

Trimming: Like all Norelcos, it does a great job trimming. The included adapter(s) handle just about everything I could imagine needing. I am a hairy guy, and have not felt any pulling or ripping of the hairs, just a clean trim.

Power: I typically get several weeks worth of trimming (every 2-3 days) on a single charge. To maintain the battery, always ensure you fully drain it before recharging. Using turbo mode drains it slightly more quickly. I can go a whole vacation without needing to recharge, which is nice, but the included travel bag is handy just in case.

So, overall I'd give it 4.5 stars, only because of the leftover hairs. It would be nice to have a slightly more powerful vacuum, but I realize it's difficult to get the hairs that are trapped in a beard. I love the trimmer, and have not seen anything else out there that would beat it.

Cute color/great fit!. I bought these locally (for about the same price) and loved them. I wore salon acrylics for many years and these are only my fourth set (third by Kiss) of DIY full coverage false nails.  On my prior (and first) set of Kiss nails I initially used the adhesive tabs rather than the glue to keep from damaging my nails. They didn't stay on really great but I think there are some good reasons for that. First, its important to find which nails fit yours exactly. If they are too small the curve will interfere with the adhesive. If they are too big they will overlap your cuticles and expose the adhesive to liquids and such. I did not file my nails to encourage adhesion.  I also did not use a primer nor did I push back my cuticles. Nevertheless, they stayed on reasonably well. The big bonus was that when it was time to take them off it just takes a short soak with acetone polish remover and they pop right off. The adhesive becomes rather like rubber cement. It comes cleanly off your natural nails as well as the acrylic ones (and you can use them again). The next time I tried nails from Kiss they were a different color but the package contents and instructions were identical. This time I wanted to see how the glue worked. Still no filing, primer, or cuticle pushing. Despite those facts the nails stuck tight. They weren't going anywhere and I'm tough on nails. I even used them to pry things.  So, if you can't tell, I'm still sort of learning and experimenting to find things that work for me.  I have some muscle control problems and the Kiss glue applicator (which is every bit as good as every other non-brush applicator) presents a bit of a problem for me.  I decided to use a non-Kiss brush-on glue for this particular set.  I lightly buffed, pushed back cuticles, cleaned with acetone, and primed.  Despite being treated delicately for a special occasion and having very limited exposure to water they started popping off in less than 24 hours.  Obviously the Kiss glue is superior.  If anyone knows where I can get Kiss glue with a brush please let me know.  Anyhow, aside from the adhesive the color is really pretty.  Enough color to be noticed but it doesn't jump out at you.  One thing I have learned during my false nail journey is that these things have a right way and a wrong way to be applied.  I always get square nails so its easy to tell now that I know to look.  The part that fits against your cuticle is the rounded end.  Also, if you want them to look real you have to push them into your cuticles a bit.  I found it a bit uncomfortable during the initial application but it faded quickly.  Well worth the final look for me.  There is one other cool feature of these nails I'd like to mention. All of them are numbered. This speeds up the nail selection process quite a bit. You just find a fit for one hand and then find the other nail with the same number. I'm going to be sure to write them down next time so I can just pick out the ones I need based on number without testing lots of them.  I continue to be really pleased with the Kiss nails and I plan to buy many of them in the future. Not only can I change my manicure frequently but I can also protect my natural nails.

I had a small bruise on my face from a cosmetic procedure, and it was driving me crazy that none of my concealers or foundations would cover it. Several friends had gotten the Boo-Boo concealer in a beauty box, and highly recommended it, so I grabbed it when I saw Amazon had it on sale.

I'm very fair, so I got the light version. Ummm, I guess I'm not as fair as I thought; they aren't kidding when they say 'fair'! This is Caspar white!

No matter. I mixed a bit of foundation in a more human shade in with the Boo-Boo, and my bruise was history (or at least until I washed my makeup off.) Very nice cover-up, no creasing, no caking, and it didn't move all day. The only issue I had, aside from how light the lightest shade was, is that it did such a good job of covering up the bruise it made the surrounding skin look naked (this is a VERY full coverage item.) Just be aware of that when you buy it.

And take them at their word for the color! I'm probably somewhere between light and medium in the Boo-Boo universe. You can always add a drop or two of your foundation to make the color more your shade.

My dad is a surgeon and my mom is a nurse so growing up I always had really good tweezers and other instruments to use for the occasional splinter etc... When I moved away from home I noticed that good tweezers and such were almost impossible to obtain unless you wanted to pay a fortune for the ones they actually use in operating rooms. The main issue I have with most tweezers is: 1) the metal at the pinching end does not align properly and thus you cannot get a good grip on a hair or splinter and 2) they are made of soft metal and therefore lack the rigidity that is required to get a good grip on the splinter or object.
THESE tweezers are awesome however! The pinching ends meet up perfectly so that if you close the tips together in front of a light, no light comes through, translating into a solid grip. The metal itself is strong and rigid as well, taking care of my second complaint with most tweezers. There is a nice glossy coating on the tweezers which makes them easy to clean and provides a good surface so your fingers don't slip off.
There are four different tweezers included and they are all great. The case it comes in is about the size of a typical wallet. My biggest fear was being left with a hideous orange color, or a bright sun yellow, which didn't happen. I'm pretty happy with the results, since I have heard how hard it is to get red out. I did wrap my hair in plastic wrap, and tried to keep it warm with a towel to improve the results. I may give it another go just to get closer to the grey, but I'm going to give it some time so I don't damage my hair. Definitely glad I went this route instead of something that may have damaged my hair.

I watched a YouTube video on how to safely dermaroll/micro-needle at home before doing it, and recommend others do the same. These were my key takeaways:
- soak the head in 91% isopropyl alcohol for 20 minutes before and after using. These needles will puncture the top layer of your skin so they need to be CLEAN.
- wash your face thoroughly with a fragrance-free and oil-free cleanser before rolling.
-roll your face methodically, about 3 swipes back and forth (6 total) per area. Then do the same in the opposite direction (ie. First side to side then up and down).
- DO NOT PUSH DOWN ON THE ROLLER. The needles are sharp enough to penetrate the top layer of your skin with very little pressure. Applying too much pressure can be very damaging.
-try to roll on a flat skin surface by holding your skin taut. Be careful around eyes, sides of nose, and lips.
- after rolling, only apply fragrance-free serum or moisturizer. Don’t use anything that you don’t already know works well with your skin. Hyalauronic acid is recommended but make sure you use it sparingly. After rolling your skin should be able to more easily absorb these minerals.

Lightweight, Easy to Use Facial Brush with 2 Speeds and Pulsing Action. I have used a Clarisonic Mia brush for more than two years, and although I like it, I've read that the Clarisonic brush can be too harsh. So, I was interested to try the Philips PureRadiance brush. First, the differences:

1. The Philips PureRadiance brush has two speeds, one is gentle and the other is a more intense option. This is a good feature, as in the winter when my skin is dry, a gentler speed is better for my skin.
2. The Philips PureRadiance brush has rotating bristles plus an pulsing feeling. The brush head is smaller than Clarisonic, so it is easy to use in small areas such as between your nose and mouth.
3. Similar to the Philips toothbrush, the PureRadiance brush has three timed sessions of 20 seconds each for three zones of your face. This is beneficial if you have a tendency to over scrub or irritate your skin.
4. The PureRadiance brush is smaller and lighter than the Clarisonic.

The PureRadiance is a different experience from the Clarisonic. It's not bad, just different. If this is your first facial brush, I think you will like the PureRadiance quite a bit. If you currently use a different brush, you'll need to compare features. If a gentle, light, easy to use brush is what you want, the Philips PureRadiance is a nice choice.

Seems like quite a lot of these Amazon users collect freebies/discounts, "review" the product and then collect more and more freebies. Or maybe there is a cash incentive? You get what you pay for. These plates are just cheaper (price-wise and quality) versions of Konad plates. You get 21 plates for about $18, and shipping is free, so that's quite an irresistible deal, but I have to say, these plates CANNOT compare to the Konad plates.
First of all, there is no safety backing on the plates, as many people have written already; the plates are very thin, and can be very sharp. I resorted to pasting the plates to index cards so it's less likely to slice into my fingers, and to prevent the plates from scratching each other.
Secondly, the designs of the plates are not as intricate and well done as the Konad plates. I have a bunch of Konad plates, and the BM designs definitely don't come close. The BM designs are not as detailed, and just are not as "pretty" as the Konad designs (but of course, you get what you pay for). Also, some of the plates I got, seems like there were manufacturing flaws. The designs on the plates appear smeared, or smudged, and when I tried to stamp them, the images do not transfer properly, if at all.
Thridly, the full nail designs don't actually fit on your whole nail (unless you have really small hands, or are a child). I learned that if I'm very precise on how I stamp, I can get away with stamping the "full nail" designs from my index to my pinky. Thumb is definitely out of the question, lest you end up with a half stamped thumb, or you're good enough to stamp in two halves (you have to really match up the designs). I've never had this problem with Konad designs.
Fourthly, some of my plates arrived with water and rust stains. I don't understand how this happens, since there is a thin Saran type film ontop the plates when you first get them. This must mean that the plates have somehow gotten wet during manufacturing process, but before the packaging process. This doens't interfere with the stamping process, but I just find it annoying to have rust and water marks on my plates.
Overall, these plates are dirt cheap (under a dollar for each plate), compared to Konad which are between $4-7 per plate, but you get what you pay for, and Bundle Monster plates definitely do NOT compare to the quality of Konad's.

The device does have the cooling feature, as many others do, which helps it not to zap too badly. It also comes with a razor and eye protection.

This IPL device works pretty much as well as any other, with none having the ability to make you completely hair-free at any point in the future. As far as the studies that I have seen, with diligent use, home IPL devices can only offer a little better than 50-60%-ish less hair.
My preferred device, which costs very little more than this one, has several attachments, including some specifically for skin rejuvenation. You do get a fancy box with this device, and it looks nice, but I don't think it provides any more or less than devices that cost much less.
I haven't found one yet that really only takes 10 minutes to do your legs, but if I ever do, that is the one that would probably take the cake! If you like fancy boxes and a sleek-looking device, I would recommend this one.

PROS:
- Unscented
- Its Natural/Aluminum-free Deodorant (As a former Peace Corps volunteer who completed my 27-month commitment, I really appreciate natural alternatives)

CONS:
- I smelled. Unlike a reviewer who mentioned how they enjoyed letting their armpits breath and bask in the naturalness, I do not, and after about 5 hours my armpits smelled, which means I had to spend the last 3 hours at my office hoping and praying others could not smell me.

- I hated applying/pasting my armpit with deodorant like a savage. Using a small wooden stick to paste deodorant to your armpit feels wrong. After a while i got 'used' to it, but I never liked it.

- I got small red rashes under my armpits. This may be due to the fact that my arms were rubbing together for the 1st time, as I had to trim my hair to get the deodorant to work for more than 2 hours.

- Its expensive AND it only lasted ONE month. Normally, each rolling stick of Gillette/OldSpice will last me at least 3 months....this is just not economical.....$11 for 3 ounces....is a very poor fiscal decision in my book.

Additions:
I really tried. I used the product until every last drop was gone. I wanted to see if my body just needed time to adjust. I noticed that the deodorant last maybe 2 hours with my little armpit hairs, so I shaved, not with a razor, with a trimmer, gave it a nice minimalist look. One month later I still smelled. Daily, I would rush home and use my Dr.Bonners to wash away the armpit funk. God forbid I actually worked up a sweat/perspired from doing something that day, then I would almost immediately smell. It was not enjoyable.

Recommendations:
- Release a version for MEN (in my Ron Swanson voice)
- Eliminate the wooden stick, release a rolling stick version
- Release a larger size, for the same cost (Seriously.)

Excellent, even for a blade-user. I bought this shaver a while ago, but I wanted to wait at least a month before writing my review, since it's supposed to take about that long before your face is used to an electric razor.
This is my first electric, and I was concerned going into it. I looked at the price of good standard blades, though, and saw how quickly an electric razor would pay for itself. I'll never go back. For the first week, the shave was not as close as I had become accustomed with using a blade. After that, though, I've gotten closer and closer shaves by the week. After a little more than a month of using the Spectra, my skin is now smooth even against the grain. I've gotten back to where I was with a blade.
The Pros:
- Shaving takes easily only half the time as it did with a straight razor.
- I can shave any time, any where. With a blade, if I tried to shave more than once per day, I'd cut myself all up into a bloody mess. With this electric, I do notice some discomfort after having shaved a second time in a day, but it gets a nice close shave. A little after shave takes care of the sting, and I'm good to go again.
- No mess. I really don't miss having to use shaving cream, even my nifty hot-lather shaving cream.
The Cons:
- Motor power seems to wind down a bit towards the end of the battery charge. It's not too bad, but it seems to take longer to shave at the end of the charge, and I don't want to charge it early for fear of damaging the battery.
- This is really a minor quibble, but I thought I'd mention it: Since this razor rinses clean under tap water, what few bits of hair are still left over are sitting in water over night. Every time I use the razor, for the first minute of shaving, it smells very strongly of old, wet hair.
Tips:
- Blade users: Apply less pressure than you're used to. I find I get a better shave when the razor is touching the skin firmly, noticibly, but not pressing in at all.
- Rinse it out every day, and turn the faucet up high. If you let it go a couple days without rinsing, it's much harder to clean out. It only takes a couple seconds, so why not?
- Shave daily. I find that if I let my beard get a little longer the shaver still does a pretty good job. However, there will always be a few hairs that grew too long, curling down, that are not lifted by the razor head. Just shave daily, when you only have stubble, to avoid this.
- Get a makeup mirror! These little mirrors are concave, magnifying your face so you can see where you've missed more easily. I mounted mine to the wall, slightly below my chin. Now I can more easily see if I've shaved my neck well.

Better than my flatiron!. I have a graduated bob and bleached (level 12) hair. This means varied lengths, from about 4" to 10", and damaged hair that must be treated very tenderly. Because I favor a smooth underswept style, I was using my flatiron to achieve that look, but first I had to blowdry my hair or my natural wave would still turn through the ironing. A double process is a pain, and the blowdrying takes away the sheen from my hair, making it look lifeless.

The brush iron is easy to hold and does not diminish the hair's sheen. I strongly recommend sectioning your hair, doing a little at a time. Don't try to take a large section and roll it...unless you are very precise, it will be easy to cross-roll as you get it out of your hair, creating a nightmare tangle.

I take a section and hold the end of the hair so the section goes straight up. Then I put the iron under the hair...the stiff bristles keep the iron awaay from my scalp, so no danger of burning myself (unlike my flatiron). I pull the section of hair down over the iron and keep it like that for about 10 seconds (on 'high', and my hair is fine) then I continuously roll the brush through the hair as I bring it down to the end. I keep rolling it as I let the end curl around and roll it up like a regular curling iron.

Because there is no upper grip, there is no danger of getting an indention in the hair. Just beware of cross-rolling the hair.

Also, keep your fingers offf the barrel. Easy to say, but I did burn a fingertip. Now I let the cool plastic end of the roller rest in my left palm for guidance, and keep my fingers well awaay.

I'll post an update if I have more observations.

Perfect little filigree cuffs. These Dreadlock Beads for Hair, Braids and Locs caught my eye. I actually wanted them for two reasons. One reason being that summer is coming and I wanted to do a slightly BOHO look with little braids without having rubber bands showing. I LOVE summer BOHO and silver filigree is just my style so these beads (which are actually more like cuffs) are perfect for me. The second reason I wanted these is that I am starting to make handmade dolls and these would be perfect for a little boho doll I am currently working through the design on. I found several good things about these little beads:

-they are lightweight so they won't weigh heavily on your hair and damage it
-they are easily opened so that you can slide your hair in and not have to 'thread' it through
-they are not large (only 8mm) or overly ornate so they add to your hair design rather than take away from it
-they can be used at the root of your hair, the middle of your hair or the end and are still comfortable to sleep on
-they come in a pack of 50 which is more than ample for your hair styles (although if you have very thick hair and are using two per braid or dread you may want to get more)
-they lock onto your hair or braid snugly

The only downside I had with these little cuffs was when I used the first one. It was my fault though as I closed it too quickly and a bit too hard, I flattened the poor little thing. Unfortunately once you flatten them they are near impossible to get round again. The next one was simpler. I had opened it gently, slid my hair through and placed my thumb and forefinger on either side of the opening and GENTLY pushed the ends back together and VOILA! perfectly round still! With each bead it got easier and easier until I didn't even think about it anymore. To get them over a rubber band simply slide your braid into the bead then slide it down over the rubber band rather than trying to open and close it enough to fit the rubber band. Also wrap the rubber band in such that it is the same length and the bead (or a little shorter) so that there is no 'belly' and it is hidden by the bead.

Overall I found these little beads to be just what I needed! I did get my first pack at a discount in exchange for a fair review and that is what I have done. I LOVE these little beads and am looking forward to getting more for myself and my creations.
