Painful and kind of flawed. Pros
• Sturdy and durable – The tweezers themselves are aluminum, but surprisingly sturdy.
• Great carrying case – Tweezers fit inside tube, just like a lipstick!
• Convenient mirror – Located inside of plastic tube that stores the tweezers.
• Easy to understand – Push a button and use.
• Light – Bright blue, useful in a way.
• Packaging – The packaging is honestly one of the best I’ve received a beauty product in. The bag is sheer with a ribbon in place for the draw string. It’s already filled with my other beauty products. The carrying case is what makes it though! It looks like a tube of lipstick, and when you remove the tweezers there’s a little mirror inside.
• Bellabe-esque spring wand – It works! It hurts like anything but man, it gets the job done. Beware areas with high density hair, it will nearly bring tears. Also, I didn’t find it effective on the outer lying hairs of my eyebrow, I believe the skin is too loose.

Cons
• Light – The button is flimsy and seems like it may break eventually. Also, when I attempted to turn the light off the first time I accidentally held down the button which actually made the light strobe. Also, it may seem silly but I felt like the light was a little too bright and washed out the area of my skin I was attacking. Finally, the light takes 3 of those watch like batteries, and I’m sorry to say that the odds of me taking time out of my day to go get these things once it dies are very slim. It does come with them included though, so for now that’s not an issue.
• Mirror – The mirror is definitely a convenience and the placement is a great idea, however, I feel like it would be more useful if the mirror was a magnifying one so I didn’t need to hold it so close to my face.
• Tweezers – The ends are not as slanted as I would like, and while I may be just tweezer challenged, I found myself chasing the same strand of hair for minutes at a time. It would be great if you could switch the tweezers that the light attaches to, but that doesn’t seem possible.

Overall, while the packaging for this product is awesome, I don’t think it’s for me. But hey, I could just be less tweezer savvy than others.

Works well. My usual sun protection is avoidance. I have sensitive, allergic, rosacea skin. I'm allergic to most chemical sunscreens, so decided that I would make my own this Spring. Actually went to a presentation by one of the big mlm essential oil companies, because they were going to present recipe for using EOs in a natural sunscreen (later research told me that EOs don't have sun prevention qualities.) The bad news is that the presentation was appalling (safety and lack of ingredient knowledge), the good news was it made me do research and take two online courses from a reputable online aromatherapy institute. One of which was a Butters & Balms course. Make a lot of my own skin products now. I had previously ought all of the ingredients to make my own sunscreen, but then decided to buy some to see how it worked for me. It did. Got one on Etsy. It was fine. There were some times during the summer that my skin was so awful that nothing wouldn't have upset it. It's a firmer consistency, I used it MANY times and barely made a dent in the jar. Bought a natural sunscreen lotion on Amazon, it had an SPF of 32. Because it contained so much of the zinc oxide, it made my face chalk white. The Tropical Sands Sunscreen only has an SPF of 8, so no white face.

The Tropical Sands All Natural Sunscreen is a lotion consistency. I'm not ready to make my own products with a water base because they need a preservative system. Lotion is easier to apply and make sure you cover the body parts completely. Probably a better consistency for sunscreen. The bottle is 8oz. It recommends application every 40 minutes if swimming or sweating. Even with the frequent application, it should still last a while. It's also the most reasonable price of all the ones I've tried.

Many sunscreens that contain non nano zinc oxide or titanium dioxide call themselves "nearly natural." Did some research because I thought they were chemicals, they are minerals. They provide a physical block rather then a chemical block. The biggest problem with the products that contain mineral blocks is that they make your face white--the more minerals, the whiter your face gets. Before the rosacea, I was light skinned, but not that porcelain white. It's December and while the weather is warmer then normal, it's not suntan weather, so my face doesn't have any other color. The Tropical Sands was fine, didn't change my skin color.

As with any new product on my face, I did a sample application. Put a little on the side where my hair would cover a reaction. It didn't make my skin reactive negatively, so I tried it on my nose and cheeks (most reactive part of my face.) I didn't have a negative reaction there. I'll definitely have to experiment with it during the prime sun time because there are times I have to be out in the sun.

I did find that using my own quick drying topcoat that these wore much better, but from the manufacturer neither base nor top coat are required.  I did not get any staining from these, which I love.  The pink and white will both be really good polishes for doing either French tip or pond manicures when you just want a sheer base, where you do a layer, do art over it, then cover it again, and more art on that layer-it gives a layered effect that is fun to do.  The color palate is a fun one, with lots of options for artwork.  These are not quick drying-more of the typical 10 minutes per layer, and I expected them to be hardened on their own, without the help of a quick drying topcoat, but that was not the case with them.

Half the cost, but more convenient than a regular Sonicare. Pros: half the cost of a Sonicare w/charger, less bulky
Cons: None so far

First of all, I should state that I have owned this product for over a year, and I am still giving it five stars.

Here's why: I had a Sonicare Advance for about three years and it worked well during that time, but at the end of those three years I had to keep it in the charger at all times or it would die in the middle of brushing. I was sick of lugging around the bulky charger any time I traveled, so when I saw the AA-battery model at Target for $40 I scooped it up.

Now instead of having to rely on an internal battery and a charger, I just keep four rechargeable AAs that I swap out when one pair dies. This isn't something I have to do very often--a pair of AAs lasts about a month (that's with two two-minute brushings a day). I have also not had any water damage, so the brush still works as great as my old Sonicare ever did. I do try not to get water on the brush and dry the entire unit whenever I finish using it. In addition, I take it apart once every two or three months and swab the O-ring with alcohol to keep it clean. This seems to be all of the maintenance needed to keep it in top condition.

So, if you want a good Sonicare brush that takes up less space and is easier to travel with, I highly recommend this model. I recommend cleaning it once in a while and trying to keep water out of the insides. I acknowledge this might not help if you get a bad unit (as many reviewers seem to have gotten), but mine has been great and I figure it can't hurt!

Eyelash growth serum, update July 2020. I have loved using false eyelashes, and now the individual lash is very popular and looks beautiful when well done, but upkeep is too expensive to include in one’s daily ablutions, because nothing is done to help keep the natural lash root attached. Therefore the lash extensions will fall off with the natural lashes that they are glued to. Maintenance of lash extensions can get expensive.

The idea of applying a growth serum-like material on the base of the target lashes seems to be the best way to go if the method actually works. I looked at many products and reviews and I chose this one to try because the price was reasonable and many of its reviews were positive.

I find that the brush to apply this serum is very, very thin, it takes a bit of practice to draw that “eyeline” of the serum in such a way to get the product only where it needs to go and not have it drip (has high viscosity) or end up on your upper eyelid from blinking (I have hooded eyelids). I am applying this on a clean dry base of lashes at bedtime. I’m a little more than a week into the application and as soon as I can see some significant lash length growth I will report back.

At this point I’m at the stage where I’m beginning to think I see some change; but I’m looking for significant change which would actually be from this method and not just staying off of the false eyelashes for a while, which could generate lashes that are filling back in. Lash enhancement using a growth serum this way that we’re talking about here is additionally the increase of the actual length of the lashes. This means a healthier lash root that stays in its root base (follicle) long enough to grow long naturally. Having long eyelashes could be very pretty even without mascara.

This blemish kit comes with six double sided tools that are made from 100% stainless steel, a zippered leather storage case with elastic loops which hold the tools in place, and an instruction sheet on how to use and care for all of the instruments. K+S Wax review: It's halfway between A.C. Fiber and Pomade, but heavy.. This review is for the K+S Wax.
*I am not being paid for any reviews, and I paid for this product.*

I have previously used American Crew Fiber, American Crew Pomade, and TIGI Bedhead.

I would say this product is in between the American Crew Fiber and Pomade.
It has the hold of Fiber, but it has more shine, closer to the Pomade. It's not over the top though, and it doesn't make your hair look too sleek or greasy.

Since this product has beeswax, that means that 1. It won't wash out of your hair with just water, because beeswax is naturally water-repellant, and 2. it's heavy. Initially, your hair may have volume (from blow-drying), but it will definitely sink because this product will weight it down. If you're looking for something that provides volume, I would go for the forming cream or clay.

Lastly, it has a strong hold once it's settled down: if I ran my hands through my hair it'd be crunchy.

This product would be great for men with short hair as it will provide texture, a little bit of shine, and hold.
I would prefer the American Crew Fiber because it doesn't have as much shine, and isn't quite as heavy.

An Improved Norelco Shaver. I, like many others I presume, have been on a lifelong search for the perfect electric shaver. Being interested in saving time in the morning and not risking the effort to shave daily with a bladed razor, I have long preferred an electric shaver and have tried everything from Remington to Braun to Norelco. The Norelco tripleheader technology was what I always came back to.

I recently purchased the Norelco Arcitec 1060 razor after reading of its improvements and seeing its new design. It is still a triple header but the floating heads now sit on a swiveling ball-type joint that allows easier and presumably closer access to one's beard in many of the former "difficult-to-reach areas". It comes with a charging stand and a travel sphere that also doubles as a charger.

After several weeks, I find my shaves are closer than with my older Norelco 8170XL Norelcoseries model and I do feel like I have more control of this razor on my face and neck. It is powerful enough to get the job done with just a few circular strokes while holding the skin stretched.

I would have preferred a model with a direct cord capability but alas, this model must be recharged to be used: obviously, when the battery goes, you will not be able to run the razor with an electrical cord while waiting for a new battery.

Also, since the floating heads sit on the flexible pedestal, there is little collection room for cut whiskers to be stored; indeed, each head needs to be opened and cleaned after every couple of shaves. Of interest is the claim that the heads can be cleaned by just rinsing them--although I have yet to bring myself to try this. There is a symbol on the front that points out when the heads need to be cleaned (rinsed) and symbols for battery life. All in all, a shaver I am still enjoying after 3 weeks.

Cremo is great, but different. I note some of the negative reviews here with interest. I am not sure that they are written in good faith, but on the assumption that they are, one complaint that I can relate to is that Cremo does not lather and that it does not shave as well as some other shaving soaps and creams. I initially had a similar reaction when I first started to use Cremo but that changed with experience, as I relate below.

I have to feel that these negative reviews are probably due to the user not knowing how to work with the product and not knowing what to expect. Cremo is not a high lathering (or even much of a low lathering) cream. If used correctly (or even incorrectly for that matter) you will definitely not get a nice white Barbasol cloud of foam on your face. What you will get is a very light, essentially transparent, coating of highly slick lubricant. And that is the other thing: with Cremo you need to use a lot (I mean a lot) of water. In fact you need to use a ratio of something like 20:1 water to product. The more water, the better, even if you think you are using so much that you are essentially washing the product off your face (you aren't). This stuff is very highly concentrated.

As stated above, I am somewhat sympathetic to the negative reviews since it took me a while to warm up to Cremo myself. But once I learned that 20:1 ratio then it all came together. And remember to re-splash water on your face between shaving with the grain and against the grain. In fact, I typically re-apply some water just going to the other side of my face. You really cannot apply too much water.

Just to spell it out, here is how to use it. Squeeze out about a half to three quarters inch of the stuff onto the tips of your fingers. Dab a little on both cheeks and then the rest on your neck. Rub into the skin (your face should already be wet). Then wet your hands with water and rub in again. Then repeat that. At this point you are ready to give it a go. If things don't seem slick enough yet, wet your hands again and rub in again. (You get the idea.)

So now that I know how to use it, what do I think of it? I think it is as good as anything out there - and I am comparing it against expensive English shave soaps, not canned foams and gels (which are clearly inferior). If you use it correctly it does provide an extremely slick surface for your razor to ride on. Remember: water!

(And just for the record, I don't work for the company, don't have any financial interest in the company, nor do any of my family or friends. These negative reviews prompted me to write this.)

Okay. To date, I have tried a variety of methods to curl my hair with minimal success. Of the heatless methods, this product is my preferred go-to, though I still haven't mastered it. My experience with this product does not impact my review - my score is based on the overall use of the product itself.

Material;
Hair health is important especially when it comes to styling.
The rod and hair ties are silk which is a definite plus. However, for the health of your hair, you are sacrificing ease. The softness of silk creates slippage and combined with the length of the rod this causes difficulty when prepping the hair.

I am not complaining about the material itself - just stating it would be nice to have a way to ensure the product stays in place during prep.

Supplies;
The clip meant to hold the rod in place while prepping isn't my favorite, but this is due to personal comfort rather than a mark against the product. It just feels like it's pulling at my hair rather than holding things in place. For those who may have a similar experience, I suggest having other types of clips handy.

The rod itself is really long, which can be beneficial to ensure all of your hair can be wrapped. However, this length gets in the way. Securing the wrapped hair proves difficult with the amount of material you have to move the hair ties over. Wearing this product during the day is going to be awkward with any sort of head movement. With that being said, the rod itself is comfortable to wear, even while sleeping. I just wish there was extra fabric at the ends to allow for tying the rod out of the way.

Use;
Lastly the instructions are basic, so I suggest the use of tutorials to find what best works for you. Some things to consider for first-timers;
- Do not use wet hair. Damp to dry works best.

- Use some sort of product to help your hair keep shape, especially if it's heavy.

- There is a learning curve. Don't give up if you don't get it right the first few times. I'm still struggling to find the best way to achieve the look I want.

With my points in mind, I do recommend this product for those seeking heatless curls. The product itself is not bad - it just takes some practice to get used to.

Another reason I think they didn’t stay on 12 hours was instead of following directions, I read somewhere that a person put the eyeliner on the the lashes while still wet and it worked better. I didn’t want to ruin my own lashes with the glue kind plus I can’t get them on good enough without adjusting them. These you can take off and adjust. This gave me confidence I lacked in doing this. Waited for a chance to buy this. Worth it.. A chiro student here. Have not used Activators of any types (Type 2 or Type 4) before, so this is my first tool. Once I got it, I used it on someone I know and it worked well! This works similarly to an activator type 2 where the tool just has to be placed at the spot that you desire.

Pros:
-The box is small, covered in foam when it arrived. Simple manual and instructions are included inside.
-This is a great tool if you decide to save some money instead of buying the 'branded' version. (Type 2 and 4)
-Lightweight
-Small, easy to carry around.
-Great quality, great materials.
-12 month warranty.
-Force is adequate and strong (at least for me, have not used activator type 2 or type 4 yet).
-Adjustment is gentle (as long as the setting is right depending on which body part you are planning to aim).
-Precise as it should be.

Cons:
-Sound of the recoil can be quite loud at times (you'll get used eventually), it is quite loud if it's near my ears.
-Recoil can be quite strong on the palm area if a higher setting is used (lower settings have lesser recoil as less force is needed), can lead to pain if you have thinner and smaller hands like me after using the medium setting for a while.
-The fingers and the palm rest can be a bit far from one another (I have smaller hands) so the recoil can be felt on the palm area (remember to take breaks).
- No carrying case included, sold separately (just a nitpick from me).

If the cons doesn't bother you too much, this is a really great tool. I have thinner and smaller hands so the experience varies.

Conclusion: This tool is worth the price that you're paying for unless you have used activators of any sort before as your experience might vary if you have used those before.
This tool is a great entry point for students/chiropractors/other people if they have not used activators before.
At least for now, I won't be able to use it as a primary tool as the recoil strains my hand and there are techniques for me to use. It might change as time goes on.

I will recommend this tool to people who use it as their secondary adjusting tool and to people who are really on a budget.

I was able to use the trimmer immediately after opening it. I watched a few YouTube videos on how to give a buzz cut and set off. My son was not in a mood for a haircut at the time after having just got back from out of state so it was a bit of a challenge. It was as if he was hula hooping with his upper body without the hoola hoop.

Halfway through the cut I felt the need to plug in the trimmer to see if it would have more power. I know the lower noise is supposed to make it not as unit imitating toward young children but it just didn't seem as powerful as a more professional trimmer. I couldn't exactly just buzz off my son's long hair in one swoop. I had to pull out some scissors and trim off the length before I could really start trimming toward the base of his head. It took awhile to get the look I desired. I used the 12 mm attachment since his hair is still very fine and I wanted some room for error in case I had to get any mistakes cleaned up by a hair stylist later. I did cut a line is his hair without the attachments on while attempting to trim behind his ear so that could illustrate that the base trimmer is effective in cleaning up hairlines. I did actually clean up his neck hairline but the way I used it kind of scratched the surface of his neck.

The design of the trimmer is simple. There's a basic indicator light that is green when turned on with a side button and it is red while charging.

Overall, I feel the trimmer is effective in doing its job. I believe for some little kids that a trimmer is scary regardless of how you design it. My son's first haircut was with scissors for that reason. It can be especially scary if you don't know what you're doing and have to take longer trying to figure it out with a new trimmer. I will give it another try when my son is in a better mood and my distraction methods work better.

As a daily tool I think it could dry out my hair, even using the conditioner they recommend. However, I was very pleasantly surprised that my hair still looked good after sleeping on it (that is a huge rarity for me), so it doesn't need to be used daily, just between washes. Regardless, it's a great tool to have for quick fix-ups or when I want a more glamorous, smooth look.

What an upgrade. I usually get packs of cheapola showercaps from the dollar store (like a six pack of plastic bags with a rubberband, you know?) but they don't last long... So I had a vinyl one that lasted longer, but was really just that same old design that was just plastic tied to your head with elastic...

This shower cap is... well, frankly, after the other ones I've used... luxurious. The material is not plastic, but more like the soft nylon on my windbreaker jacket. It's much quieter when I'm in the shower, which makes for a more peaceful bathing experience. It is also more comfortable, as the headband is more fitted. It's especially comfortable if you wear it over your ears... there's no pressure anywhere, but it still keeps your hair dry. I, personally, like to have my ears "out," so there is some pressure to the top of my ears where the headband sits, but I don't mind it.

The headband does stretch a bit for head size, but not as much as you might be used to if you've used shower caps with elastic bands. I kind of liked this... It makes it easier to get all my hair in it. I flip my head upside down over the shower cap, and the cap just kind of catches my hair like a bucket, and I can just tuck in any stragglers before flipping my head back up. If you need to tighten the headband just a little bit, you can re-tie the bow for a slight adjustment.

No shower cap is going to be completely, perfectly water tight. You're always going to get a little bit of water around the edges unless you're really careful in the shower and take pains to avoid direct spray. I use a shower cap when I take a shower before bed and don't want to go to sleep with wet hair... a little bit of moisture doesn't bother me, as I'm not trying to protect a hairstyle or anything. I really just like the comfort and feel of this cap a lot!

French green clay: a miracle substance with multiple health benefits?. Green clay was first quarried in southern France, where producers had a global monopoly until identical deposits were discovered in North America and in China. The green color is a combination of ferrous oxides and decomposed kelp and other algae. Other ingredients identified include calcium, magnesium, potassium, manganese, dolomite, phosphorus, zinc, aluminum (yes, and it has health benefits!), silicon, copper, selenium, cobalt and a rare mineral called ‘montmorillonite’.

Whereas green clay has been used for decades as a cosmetic treatment, especially on the face, its application for internal use by natural health practitioners is less well known. The way you take it is: sprinkle a level teaspoonful in a glass of water, stir it in and leave it around 8 hours to sit (overnight, for example), before drinking it half an hour before food.

The clay absorbs free toxins in the gut, binds with them and passes them out of the body in regular bowel movements. It attracts molecules and pathogenic organisms like a magnet by a process called ‘adsorbency’ (NOT absorbency). By this method the clay eradicates fungi like candida, all kinds of bacteria, parasites, viruses, chemical residues – especially heavy metals - and other toxic materials.

It’s commonly claimed that green clay should never be mixed using a metal spoon, or stored in a metal container. Wooden, ceramic or glass spoons and containers should be used. The belief that the clay loses its adsorbent qualities through prolonged contact with metal has some scientific basis, because it has been found to be highly effective in removing heavy metals in non-organic environments. However, if you’re just using a metal teaspoon to spoon the clay into a glass and stir it for a few seconds, that should be fine. There is also a counter-indication for people on prescription medicines like anti-hypertension drugs; because of the clay’s adsorbency its presence in the gut may interfere with the body’s abilities to absorb these medicines as intended. Best consult your doctor or medical herbalist about this.

I have combination skin and my biggest issue with serums is that a lot of them tend to dry my skin out. This serum does not. It keeps my face feeling moisturized. I apply it only at night after I tone my face. I press/pat this all over my face and neck. I use about 3.5 pumps to cover my entire face and neck. This product dries extremely fast. So you need to work in sections when you apply it to your face. For example, I apply it to my left side, then my right side, my forehead and eyes and then my neck. If you try to apply it all over your face at once it will dry before you get it properly spread out. It leaves a light film on your face but once it dries completely the residue is gone.

A lot of people complain about the pump not allowing small amounts to be squirt out. It's one full squirt or nothing. I found this to be true at first but after a few uses I now know how to partially press the pump down allowing me to get a customized amount of product out. The trick is: You need to firmly hold onto the sides of the pump with your middle finger and thumb (the pressure from your fingers slow the pump down), while your index finger slowly presses the pump down.

Overall, I like it for what it is. I haven't seen a noticeable difference in my smile lines but hopefully it's doing it's job of preventing wrinkles.

Leaves You Feeling Silky Smooth. Like another reviewer, this was not an item I would have selected myself. I received it as a gift from a friend and was hesitant to use it out of fear that it would have an overpowering floral smell due to the lavender. However, the bar ended up being a pleasant surprise, and I will likely buy it again.

Since I don't like too many bubbles in my bath and, more importantly, like stretching my Lush products as much as possible due to the cost, I cut the bar into fourths. I found it to be a lot harder to cut than most Lush products, so if you're going to cut it, use a really strong knife and be ready for it to blow apart a bit as you slice through. (It's pretty crumbly.)

What I like about this bar is that, even though it's not very bubbly -- even as someone who cuts bars, I usually get more from others than this one -- it leaves a wonderful silky feeling on your body. I love that, even in the water, I can feel it on my legs, and not in an annoying greasy way at all. It's so relaxing! I usually put cocoa butter on my legs after shaving, and I don't need to do anything after using this bar. It has some sort of wonderful lotion quality about it that I adore. More than the scent or bubbles, that is the reason I will purchase it for myself in the future.

The only objection I have is that it seems to melt a bit more than other bubble bars. I've kept it in a sealed container in a cool area, but it just doesn't keep well. If you're going to cut it, be sure to use the other pieces within a couple weeks at the most. And, like all bubble bars, don't get it wet unless you're going to use it right away, because even the tiniest bit of moisture gets it going.

About this book .... The first edition of The Presence came out in 1945 and went through two printings. Berthold von Schenk had by then been a LCMS parish pastor for 27 years and was serving his third parish, Our Saviour Lutheran Church in the Bronx, New York. The material came from years of sermons, lectures and retreat meditations. The Presence is his confession of what the Holy Eucharist means to him and what it can mean for us: the actual presence and self-giving of the living Christ.

The 65 years since its original publication have not diminished the power of The Presence to illuminate the well-known narratives and doctrines of our faith in striking ways. It would be a rare pastor or layperson who reads it through without recognizing thereafter holy ground not seen before in worship and life, and without an ever-deepening love for Holy Communion.
This edition is an updated printing of von Schenk's original 1945 edition. Footnotes and an introduction are provided by The Rev. Paul Robert Sauer, current pastor of Our Saviour Lutheran Church in the Bronx, New York.
